abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions are sized to the app's real variation and an Items section would reuse section/descriptionList/count/cardList/speciesCards/getResource almost entirely; the gaps are home's bespoke lookup maps and no shared type-label or card-sorting helper.

findings.issue: Route regexes are duplicated between the client router (main.ts:19-27) and the server's 404 probe (server.mjs:34-38); adding, renaming or removing a route requires two matching edits and the two tables can silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Export one route table (pattern + resource name + loader) from a shared module and have server.mjs import it (or generate its table from it), so a route is defined once.

findings.issue: speciesCards assumes the Pokémon reference's ID equals the species ID (species.get(id), spriteUrl(id)); it relies on the spec's guarantee that a species' default Pokémon shares its ID and would show a wrong sprite/dex number or drop the card entirely on an API where default varieties have their own IDs (as the real PokeAPI does, e.g. deoxys-normal = 10001).
findings.suggestion: Resolve the reference to a species (by fetching the Pokémon, or by a species lookup keyed by Pokémon name) and derive both the sprite URL and dex number from the species, keeping the assumption in one named function.

findings.issue: idFromUrl is re-implemented as an inline regex here and at home.ts:43 instead of using format.ts:18.

The 'English type label with humanized fallback' resolution (types.get(name) ?? humanize(name)) is repeated in move.ts:22, pokemon.ts:31, types.ts:25 and home.ts:86, so a label-rule change means four edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a typeLabeler(names) helper (or extend typeNames to return labels) in api.ts/components.ts and use it in all four places.

findings.issue: Card ordering is decided in two places — speciesCards sorts by id (components.ts:79) while home relies on speciesList's sort (api.ts:150) before slicing pages, so a name-sort change touches both.
findings.suggestion: Add one sortCards/comparator helper in components.ts and have home use the same card-list construction path as the other pages.

findings.issue: Data shaping (pokemonTypes and speciesGeneration lookup maps, ~18 lines) lives inside the home page component rather than the data layer, and would be rewritten if any other page needs the same lookups.
findings.suggestion: Move these derived maps into api.ts alongside speciesList/allTypes so the data layer owns the data shape.

findings.issue: pageStatus hardcodes the /api/v2/ prefix and resource names ('pokemon-species', 'move', …) that also appear in each page's getResource call, so a resource rename or path change needs edits in server.mjs and the page modules.
findings.suggestion: Fold these names into the shared route table from finding 1 so each resource name is defined once.

summary: A small, well-factored vanilla-TS app: pages are self-contained modules, all data access and caching sit behind api.ts, and the shared view helpers (section, cardList/speciesCards, sortableTable) are designed around the app's actual variation, so the required scenarios are mostly one-or-two-file changes. The main editability costs are the route table duplicated between main.ts and server.mjs, the ID-identity assumption inside speciesCards, and a handful of small duplicated patterns (type-label fallback, URL id parsing, card ordering). I'd merge it with the two medium findings addressed or tracked.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete ability.ts, drop the import+route in main.ts (6,22), delete the Abilities section in pokemon.ts (93-111) and the server route entry (server.mjs:37). No nav link exists and no dead code remains, but the server-side edit is easy to miss since it lives outside src/.

scenarios.change: Fix the sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Sprite URL is derived from the card id in pokemonCard (components.ts:47) via spriteUrl (api.ts:125), and the id is resolved from the Pokémon reference in speciesCards (components.ts:72-77), which every non-home list uses; home already passes species ids. One fix covers all lists, but it touches the two ends (id resolution and URL construction) rather than one line.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: speciesCards' sort (components.ts:79) covers move/ability/type lists, but home orders cards implicitly via speciesList's id sort (api.ts:150) and its own inline CardData construction (home.ts:84-91), and pagination slices depend on that order. Two files, and you'd want to introduce a shared sortCards helper first to avoid leaving two orderings again.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: Most of the Moves shape is reusable rather than copyable: getResource, Page, section, descriptionList, count, englishName/humanize/orMissing, speciesCards/cardList and the router pattern. You write one new page module, add an Item interface, two route lines, one server route line and a nav link in index.html — but the doubled route tables (finding 1) mean two of those edits are boilerplate re-declaration.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Client-side the base URL is one constant (api.ts:11-13) used by get and spriteUrl, and caching is one Map in one function (api.ts:128-145); the server injects the URL through a single seam (server.mjs:34). Only the /api/v2 prefix and resource names appear again in server.mjs:44, so a path scheme change is a two-file edit.
